sections.h2: What is kept at the Grand Traverse County Register of Deeds in Traverse City?
sections.html:
Every deed, mortgage, land contract and lien filed against land in Grand Traverse County ends up in this office. The public can search every file. Images are indexed back to 1966, and a clerk can pull older papers from as early as 1853 when given a liber and page.

Staff will not supply a blank deed or coach you through writing one. The county points owners toward a Michigan real property attorney, a title company, or a self-completed deed, and cautions that downloaded forms sometimes fail the recording rules.

The county itself spans 601 square miles, nearly a quarter of it water, and borrows its name from the bay at Traverse City. Its first European mission, at Old Mission, dates to 1839. The area was carved out in 1840 as Omeena County and reorganized as Grand Traverse in 1851. The Census Bureau estimates 96,729 people for 2025, more than any other county in Northern Michigan.

sections.h2: What will a seller pay at the Grand Traverse County recording counter?
sections.html:
A deed, mortgage or lis pendens costs $30.00 to file, however many sheets it has. Write mailed checks to Register of Deeds or GTROD and tuck in a stamped return envelope, or add $3.00 so the office can cover postage.

Charges posted by the Grand Traverse County Register of Deeds
ItemCharge
One deed, mortgage or similar instrument$30.00
Each additional instrument assigned or discharged$3
Treasurer tax certification, warranty deeds$5 for up to 25 parcels, then $0.20 per parcel
Photocopy at the counter$1.00 per page, certified copies $5.00 extra

These figures rest on MCL 600.2567. The county's schedule carries an October 1, 2016 effective date, so phone the office before writing a check for a large package.

sections.h2: How does Grand Traverse County work out the transfer tax on a sale?
sections.html:
The recorder rounds the price up to the next $500 and applies two rates. The county rate is $1.10 for each $1,000, which is the 55 cents per $500 that MCL 207.504 sets for counties of this size. The state rate is $7.50 for each $1,000, the $3.75 per $500 in MCL 207.525. A buyer or seller therefore pays $8.60 per $1,000 of rounded value.

The county works through a $110,100 sale: rounded to $110,500, the state share is $828.75, the county share is $121.55, and the sum is $950.30. Nudge the price to $110,501 and the base becomes $111,000 with a $954.60 bill. At the county's median home value of $339,400 the base would be $339,500 and the tax about $2,919.70.

  • State the full price on the deed, or attach a value affidavit.
  • Write any claimed exemption on the instrument.
  • Exemption lists live in MCL 207.505 (county) and MCL 207.526 (state).
  • Typical exemptions: price under $100, foreclosure deeds, transfers from parent to child or grandchild, and quitclaims fixing a title defect.

sections.h2: Why does the County Treasurer have to sign off before a warranty deed is recorded?
sections.html:
MCL 211.135 bars the register from recording a warranty deed or land contract until the treasurer certifies that no tax liens exist and that five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim without a warranty covenant is excepted.

The Treasurer sits at 400 Boardman Avenue, Suite 104, Traverse City, and answers at 231-922-4735. Ask early for the certification so the closing is not held up waiting on it.

sections.h2: How fast does unpaid tax turn into a lost property in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
On March 1 after the bill year, unpaid tax passes from the township, city or village treasurer to the County Treasurer. Until then, current bills are paid locally between July 1 and the end of February.

Two years of delinquency end the owner's rights. The first year adds a 4% fee and 1% interest per month. Then the parcel is forfeited, interest climbs to 1.5% monthly back to the original delinquency, and a $175 title search plus notice fees get stacked on. A certificate of forfeiture is recorded at the Register of Deeds, so buyers' title searches pick it up. A year after forfeiture, on March 31, the county forecloses, and the county describes that step as final.

  • Partial payments cut the interest that continues to build, as long as the last one lands before foreclosure.
  • Owners hear five times: two letters, two certified letters and one in-person delivery.
  • If the county auction brings more than the debt, the former owner files a Notice of Claim by July 1 and asks the court for the extra money the following February.

The county also reminds homeowners that a lender holding escrow can overlook a bill, especially right after a refinance, and the owner remains responsible.

sections.h2: Where do sellers find homes in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
The county is the heart of Northern Michigan. Traverse City is the only city and the county seat, with the villages of Fife Lake and Kingsley and the unincorporated places of Interlochen, Grawn and Chums Corner around it. Interlochen is home to the Interlochen Center for the Arts, a boarding school.

Water shapes the map. Long Lake is the biggest inland lake, the Boardman River runs west into West Bay at Traverse City, and the Old Mission Peninsula juts 17 miles into Grand Traverse Bay inside Peninsula Township. The Pere Marquette State Forest covers part of the south. A parcel on the peninsula, by a lake or in town records through the same county office, whatever its township. Seven counties touch this one: Antrim, Kalkaska, Missaukee, Wexford, Manistee, Benzie and Leelanau, and a deed for land in any of them goes to that county's own register instead.

Population climbed from 86,986 in 2010 to 95,238 in 2020 and 96,729 in the 2025 estimate, a gain of about 10,000 residents in fifteen years.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about home values in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau puts the median owner-occupied home at $339,400, with 77.2% of homes lived in by their owners. Median household income is $81,647, median rent is $1,288, and 25.1% of residents are 65 or older. The county counts 40,287 households on 464 square miles of land.

Values like these make the transfer tax a real line on a settlement statement. A seller carrying tenants, repairs or back taxes should order the treasurer's certification and a payoff letter first, so the title company can hand the register a clean deed.

faqs.q: What is the filing fee for a deed in Grand Traverse County?
faqs.a: $30.00 per document, whatever the page count. A sale adds transfer tax, and a warranty deed adds a $5 treasurer certification.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax does a Grand Traverse County sale pay?
faqs.a: $8.60 for every $1,000 of price rounded up to the next $500: $7.50 to the state and $1.10 to the county. A $110,500 base owes $950.30.

faqs.q: Can a deed be mailed to the Grand Traverse County register?
faqs.a: Yes. Enclose a check payable to Register of Deeds or GTROD plus a stamped, self addressed envelope, or add $3.00 for postage and handling.

faqs.q: When do overdue taxes move to the Grand Traverse County Treasurer?
faqs.a: March 1 after the bill year. The county then adds a 4% fee and 1% interest each month, and forfeiture follows a year later.

faqs.q: Will the Grand Traverse County register help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office provides no blank deeds and no drafting advice, so turn to an attorney or a title company.
